sections.t: Addressed to Valentinus and the Monks of Adrumetum, and Completed in One Book. Written in a.d. 426 or a.d. 427.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter I [I.]-The Occasion and Argument of This Work.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 2 [II]-Proves the Existence of Free Will in Man from the Precepts Addressed to Him by God.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 3.-Sinners are Convicted When Attempting to Excuse Themselves by Blaming God, Because They Have Free Will.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 4.-The Divine Commands Which are Most Suited to the Will Itself Illustrate Its Freedom.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 5.-He Shows that Ignorance Affords No Such Excuse as Shall Free the Offender from Punishment; But that to Sin with Knowledge is a Graver Thing Than to Sin in Ignorance.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 6 [IV.]-God's Grace to Be Maintained Against the Pelagians; The Pelagian Heresy Not an Old One.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 7.-Grace is Necessary Along with Free Will to Lead a Good Life.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 8.-Conjugal Chastity is Itself the Gift of God.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 9.-Entering into Temptation. Prayer is a Proof of Grace.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 10 [V.]-Free Will and God's Grace are Simultaneously Commended.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 11.-Other Passages of Scripture Which the Pelagians Abuse.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 12.-He Proves Out of St. Paul that Grace is Not Given According to Men's Merits.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 13 [VI.]-The Grace of God is Not Given According to Merit, But Itself Makes All Good Desert.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 14.-Paul First Received Grace that He Might Win the Crown.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 15.-The Pelagians Profess that the Only Grace Which is Not Given According to Our Merits is that of the Forgiveness of Sins.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 16 [VII.]-Paul Fought, But God Gave the Victory: He Ran, But God Showed Mercy.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 17·-The Faith that He Kept Was the Free Gift of God,
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 18.-Faith Without Good Works is Not Sufficient for Salvation.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 19 [VIII.]-How is Eternal Life Both a Reward for Service and a Free Gift of Grace?
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 20.-The Question Answered. Justification is Grace Simply and Entirely, Eternal Life is Reward and Grace.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 21 [IX.]-Eternal Life is "Grace for Grace."
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 22 [X.] -Who is the Transgressor of the Law? the Oldness of Its Letter. The Newness of Its Spirit.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 23 [XI.]-The Pelagians Maintain that the Law is the Grace of God Which Helps Us Not to Sin.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 24 [XII.] - Who May Be Said to Wish to Establish Their Own Righteousness."God's Righteousness," So Called, Which Man Has from God.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 25 [XIII.]- as Thelawisnot,so Neither is Our Nature Itself that Grace by Which We are Christians.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 26. - the Pelagians Contend that the Grace, Which is Neither the Law Nor Nature, Avails Only to the Remission of Past Sins, But Not to the Avoidance of Future Ones.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 27 [XIV.]-Grace Effects the Fulfilment of the Law, the Deliverance of Nature, and the Suppression of Sin's Dominion.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 28.-Faith is the Gift of God.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 29. - God is Able to Convert Opposing Wills, and to Take Away from the Heart Its Hardness.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 30.-The Grace by Which the Stony Heart is Removed is Not Preceded by Good Deserts, But by Evil Ones.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 31 [XV.] - Free Will Has Its Function in the Heart's Conversion; But Grace Too Has Its.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 32 [XVI.] - in What Sense It is Rightly Said That, If We Like, We May Keep God's Commandments.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 33 [XVII.]-A Good Will May Be Small and Weak; An Ample Will, Great Love. Operating and Cooperating Grace.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 34. - the Apostle's Eulogy of Love. Correction to Be Administered with Love.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 35.-Commendations of Love.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 36.-Love Commended by Our Lord Himself.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 37 [XVIII.]-The Love Which Fulfils the Commandments is Not of Ourselves, But of God.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 38.-We Would Not Love God Unless He First Loved Us. The Apostles Chose Christ Because They Were Chosen; They Were Not Chosen Because They Chose Christ.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 39.-The Spirit of Fear a Great Gift of God.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 40 [XIX.]-The Ignorance of the Pelagians in Maintaining that the Knowledge of the Law Comes from God, But that Love Comes from Ourselves.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 41 [XX.]-The Wills of Men are So Much in the Power of God, that He Can Turn Them Whithersoever It Pleases Him.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 45 [XXI]-God Does Whatsoever He Wills in the Hearts of Even Wicked Men.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 43.-God Operates on Men's Hearts: to Incline Their Wills Whithersoever He Pleases.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 44 [XXII.] - Gratuitous Grace Exemplified in Infants.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 45 [XXIII]-Thereason Way One Person is Assisted by Grace, and Another is Not Helped, Must Be Referred to the Secret Judgments of God.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will

sections.t: Chapter 46 [XXIV.] -Understanding and Wisdom Must Be Sought from God.
path: A Treatise on Grace and Free Will
